mechanism_claims.claim_text: Prior NCR247 work cited in the paper supports cytosolic entry and interaction with FtsZ/ribosomal proteins; this paper uses that as NCR247 background rather than newly quantifying those interactions for every derivative.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: NCR247 parent peptide and NCR247C context
mechanism_claims.limitations: Not promoted to direct mechanism for all chimeric derivatives because the statement is background/prior-work context.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: NCR247C-X2-StrepII directly pulled down many E. coli cytosolic proteins, predominantly ribosomal/translation proteins, supporting a direct intracellular protein-binding mechanism for peptide G.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=15:The Chimeric Peptide G: NCR247C-X2-StrepII Interacts With Many E. coli Proteins

mechanism_claims.limitations: Proteomic binding partners support interaction context but do not by themselves quantify killing potency.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: NCR247C-X2-StrepII also pulled down fewer E. coli membrane-fraction proteins including outer/inner membrane components and efflux-pump proteins, supporting membrane-protein interaction context for the X2-containing chimera.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=15:The Chimeric Peptide G: NCR247C-X2-StrepII Interacts With Many E. coli Proteins

mechanism_claims.limitations: The paper frames these as likely binding partners; exact causal contribution to killing is not separately quantified.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The X2/truncated mastoparan fusion is discussed as improving antimicrobial efficacy while avoiding the hemolytic activity of full transportan/mastoparan-like sequences.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: X2-containing chimeras F, G, and H
mechanism_claims.limitations: Inferred from activity/toxicity pattern and discussion, not a standalone direct membrane disruption assay in this paper.
